answer: Orange dotted underlines mark terms that the article’s [Glossary](/help/mode-glossary) has defined. They appear in **every mode**, including Plain, once the glossary exists. Point at one to read its card, and use the card’s **Open glossary** button for the full entry. They are not your own highlights — yours are yellow, green, blue or pink.

You can do it two ways, both under **Access & sharing** on the article's Metadata page. A **private link** (press **Create a link**, then tick that you have the right to share the text) lets anyone you send it to read the article without an account, and it isn't listed anywhere. Making it **public** (press the padlock, then **Share it**) lets anyone read it and lists it on the public shelf.

Note that sending the article's ordinary address lets nobody in, and visitors can read your comments and bookmarks but cannot write or start AI work. See [Sharing an article, and the public shelf](/help/sharing).

Skim is a route through an article's quotes that takes you a little deeper each time round. Every stop is the author's own sentence, in its place, with a short cue for what to look for — so it gives you the shape of a piece fast without putting a summary in place of the text.

You choose how deep to go: **Gist** is a handful of stops, **More** about a dozen, **Most** a larger share. Use the **‹** and **›** buttons at the top, or the **←** and **→** keys, to step from stop to stop.

To work out the route, Skim reads the article's quotes and key ideas (and makes them first if they are not there yet), planned around what you said you want from the article. See [Skim](/help/mode-skim).

No. Your allowance counts the articles you **add**, not what you do with them afterwards — opening modes, generating them, chatting and re-running them are all included. The only other thing that counts is switching an article to **High-powered AI**. See [Plans](/help/plans) and [Does opening a mode use up my allowance?](/help/questions#faq-does-a-mode-use-my-allowance).

A summary is written the first time you ask for it, and **that usually takes seconds and can take a minute or more** — the work runs only while a Spideryarn tab is open, so if you closed every tab it pauses until you come back ([Waiting for a mode](/help/waiting-and-cost)).

Two things worth checking:

- **Which way you got there.** Arriving by a link or with Back does not start it — you should see an empty panel with a button to start it. Summary's **Thread** is the exception: on your own article it starts writing as soon as you open it.
- **Whose article it is.** On someone else's shared article you see only what has already been made; you cannot start anything new.

Once it is written it is kept, so opening it again is instant. If it still never appears, send it with the **Feedback** button ([Feedback](/help/feedback)).

That’s the **scroll box**, the mark in the spine that shows what is on your screen. Its orange top and bottom edges mark the part of the article you can see, and its height shows how much of the article fits on one screen; it moves as you scroll. The spine itself is a map of the whole article, each part as tall as it is long — see [Reading the spine](/help/spine).

Yes. On an article’s Metadata page, **Export this article** downloads a zip of everything we hold for it — the text as we read it, and everything built on it, such as the glossary, quotes, comments and chats — as plain files you can open without Spideryarn. The original page or PDF and the images are not included. Your notes are otherwise private unless you share the article. See [Your data: export, archive, delete](/help/your-data) and [Comments and bookmarks](/help/comments).

Yes. Spideryarn works on a phone or tablet, though it works best on a large screen. On a narrow window a mode’s panel covers the article instead of sitting beside it, and turning the phone to landscape often gives room for both. A few things work differently by touch: tap twice on the spine (first tap shows the section’s card, second goes there), tap twice on a link, and tap a paragraph to show its margin controls. If you add it to your phone’s home screen there is no browser Back button, so use the **↩ back to** button above the bottom bar. See [Phones and tablets](/help/touch).

Summary reformule le texte en mots simples, en **Brief**, **Fuller** ou en **Thread**, et chaque paragraphe renvoie aux passages sur lesquels il repose — mais il laisse tomber le raisonnement ([Summary](/help/mode-summary)). Skim vous fait parcourir l’article par étapes : chaque arrêt est la phrase de l’auteur, à sa place, avec une courte indication de ce qu’il faut y chercher, et la route s’approfondit à chaque passage ([Skim](/help/mode-skim)).

Autrement dit, Summary vous dit ce que dit le texte ; Skim vous y conduit, sans le remplacer.

Servez-vous de Summary pour décider si l’article vaut votre temps ou pour vérifier les points principaux, et de Skim quand vous voulez la forme d’un article rapidement en restant dans les mots de l’auteur ([Which mode when](/help/modes)).

The Help pages don't mention EPUB or Kindle files. Adding an article accepts a PDF, or a web page saved as HTML — paste a web address or upload one of those files on your shelf ([Adding an article](/help/adding-articles)). If you want EPUB support, send the suggestion with the **Feedback** button ([Telling us something](/help/feedback)).

The Help pages don't say anything about a student discount. What they do say about cost is under [Plans](/help/plans): your allowance counts the articles you add, and everything you do with them afterwards — modes, chat, questions, re-running — is included. I can't see anything about discounts there, so the best thing is to ask the people who make Spideryarn directly with the **Feedback** button ([Feedback](/help/feedback)).

No: notes are kept per person, not shared live. Each reader marks their own copy, and on someone else's shared article the margin can show their existing comments or bookmarks, but you cannot add a bookmark, start a chat or use the **?** there — see [The margin beside each paragraph](/help/gutter) and [Comments and bookmarks](/help/comments).

If you want somebody else to read the same article, you can share it; visitors can read your comments but not add or change any — see [Sharing an article, and the public shelf](/help/sharing).

The Help pages don't describe an API for driving Spideryarn from your own scripts, so I can't tell you whether one exists. The closest thing the pages cover is adding a page from its address — `/add/` followed by the full URL, which makes a bookmarklet easy ([Adding an article](/help/adding-articles)) — and the command bar, which takes typed or spoken requests in the app ([Keyboard shortcuts](/help/keyboard)).

If you need a definite answer, the **Feedback** button sends the question to the people who make Spideryarn ([Feedback](/help/feedback)).
